r: Single word for viruses, worms, trojans etc.: software **designed to disrupt, damage or gain unauthorised access** to a computer (not merely buggy software)
"**Vital Information Resources Under Siege**"; a program that **replicates itself**, **attaches to files** and spreads from computer to computer
Via **images, audio/video files, downloads, attachments**; infects storage such as a **pen drive**, not a display or keyboard
A fault in a program that stops it working correctly
**John von Neumann** (1949 theory of self-reproducing automata)
**Attaches to files**, reproduces and spreads; the user must run the infected file
Uses the **network to send copies of itself without user action**; needs no host program
**Looks like legitimate software**, tricks the user into installing it, then acts like a virus/worm; no self-replication; backdoor
Secret surveillance; steals passwords, banking data
Unwanted ads; bundled with free/pirated software
Administrator-level access; **modifies the host OS to hide malware**; hardest to detect
Network of hijacked "zombie" devices for DDoS, spam

0.x: **Antivirus** software: McAfee, Kaspersky, Avast, **Webroot**, Norton; a rootkit is malware.
Viruses, worms and trojans all threaten **electronic payment systems**.
Spreads over the network by itself without user action = **worm**; disguised as genuine software, no self-replication = **trojan**.

1.x: **Cyber attack** = any attempt to harm, damage or threaten a computer system or network.

**Identical e-mail sent repeatedly** to one address to overflow it
Capturing data packets on a network
**Denial of Service**: **flooding** a server with fake traffic so genuine users **cannot access** it; DDoS uses many machines (botnet)
Secretly intercepts/alters communication between two parties
Malicious database code via website input fields
